§ 02 — Method

How a lesson runs.

01 / 04

01

Diagnose

A short, unmarked check at the start of every topic. We're not grading — we're looking for the exact line where the working goes wrong.

02

Teach

Whiteboard first, notes second. One idea at a time, with the "why" before the "how" — so the method still makes sense under exam pressure.

03

Drill

Graded question sets, easy to nasty. Students work, we walk the room. Mistakes get fixed on the spot, not three weeks later on a test.

04

Review

Every few weeks we loop back with timed past-paper questions. Parents get a short note on what's solid and what still needs work.

§ 05 — Questions

Things parents usually ask.

Should my child take Add Maths at all?+

If they're comfortable with algebra and aiming for sciences, engineering, economics or anything quantitative after school — usually yes. If basic algebra is still shaky, fix that first in Maths. We'll tell you honestly after the trial.

Which syllabus do you follow?+

We teach to the student's actual exam board and use their past papers. The topics overlap heavily anyway — the difference is mostly in question style, and we train for that specifically.

What happens in the free trial?+

A normal lesson, plus a 15-minute diagnostic at the start. Afterwards you get a short written summary of where your child is and what we'd work on first. No obligation.

Do you set homework?+

Yes, but not much — around 30–45 minutes a week of targeted questions. It's checked at the start of the next lesson, so it actually gets done.

Online or in person?+

Both. Group classes are in person. One-to-one can be either — online sessions use a shared digital whiteboard and a pen tablet, so it still feels like working on paper.
